info.bio: Ian Broudie, nacido el 4 de agosto de 1958 en Liverpool, es un personaje de largo recorrido en la música del Reino Unido. En tiempos de la New Wave formó parte como guitarrista de BIG IN JAPAN, un grupo post punk aparecido en 1977 en el cual tambien estaba la cantante Jayne Casey (Pink Military), Holly Johnson (Futuro líder de FRANKIE GOES TO HOLLYWOOD) y, entre otros componentes, Broudie (Quien con posterioridad tocaría la batería en Siouxsie and The Banshees).

scenes.name: Brit-pop y post-pop
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Como tantas veces, el fenómeno más publicitado es el menos interesante: un «brit-pop» de grupos terriblemente parecidos y tediosos, sin apenas imaginación. Lo anticipan Lightning Seeds, La's, Teenage Fanclub y Heavenly; estalla con Boo Radleys, Blur (Parklife) y Oasis (el «farol» que mejor personifica la moda). Suede y el glam-pop (Super Furry Animals, Placebo), las excepciones de High Llamas (Hawaii) y Supergrass, el revival mod (Ocean Colour Scene, Wildhearts), Elastica, Sleeper, las Spice Girls; Trembling Blue Stars, Tindersticks, Delgados. El post-pop de Radiohead, «la banda más publicitada y sobrevalorada de la década», cuyo OK Computer es una obra maestra del falso vanguardismo; Coldplay, Travis.

podcast.title: Formation and Early Projects
podcast.body: The Lightning Seeds were formed in Liverpool in 1989 by local music veteran Ian Broudie, initially as a studio project for their first two albums. "They were formed in Liverpool in 1989 by a local music vet named Ian Brody. It was originally just a studio project, and it was, for the first two albums."

podcast.body: Starting with their third album, Ian Broudie needed to take The Lightning Seeds on the road for live performances. "Starting with the third, Brody needed to take the whole thing on the road."

podcast.title: UK Success vs. North American Status
podcast.body: The Lightning Seeds are not considered one-hit wonders in the UK, where they had a series of hit singles, including a number one in 1998 (an official World Cup song). However, in North America, only "Pure" achieved lasting recognition. "For North America, though, only two songs cut through, but only one really seems to have hung on over the decades."
